root_cause.text: The Arm Ethos-U command stream parser in `drivers/accel/ethosu/ethosu_gem.c` masked `NPU_SET_IFM_REGION` with `0x7f` instead of `0x7`, allowing userspace to set `st.ifm.region` to values up to 127 and later index fixed-size `region_size[]`/`output_region[]` arrays out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;` to `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7;`, and the CVE/commit notes that `region_size[]` and `output_region[]` are sized to `NPU_BASEP_REGION_MAX` (8) while `feat_matrix_length()` and `calc_sizes()` use `fm->region` directly as an array subscript.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix IFM region parsing to mask the field to its correct 3-bit range.
intent_record.what: The mask applied when handling NPU_SET_IFM_REGION was changed from 0x7f to 0x7 before assigning to st.ifm.region.
intent_record.how: This narrows the accepted region value from 7 bits to 3 bits, preventing higher-order bits from being stored and ensuring only the intended region range is used during command stream validation.

grouping_result.intent: Fix IFM region parsing to mask the field to its correct 3-bit range.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the vulnerability root cause: it corrects IFM region parsing by masking the field to the proper 3-bit range, preventing out-of-bounds indexing from oversized region values.

candidates.rationale: This masks the IFM region field to 7 bits instead of the intended 3 bits, allowing values up to 127 and causing later out-of-bounds indexing into fixed-size region arrays.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement masks the IFM region with 0x7f, permitting values up to 127 instead of the required 3-bit range. That allows userspace-controlled out-of-bounds indexing later into fixed-size region arrays.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this function body. In the command parser, `NPU_SET_IFM_REGION` is handled as `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;`, which matches the root cause: masking with `0x7f` instead of `0x7` allows values up to 127. This is the exact bad assignment that later feeds array indexing in the same file, e.g. `info->region_size[dma->region]`, `info->region_size[fm->region]`, and `info->output_region[st->ofm.region]`. The fix is not present here because the code still uses `0x7f` for IFM region, while only OFM/IFM2/weights/DMA use `0x7` or similar bounds masking.
